newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks ended Thursday up but sharply off their day highs as the market searched around for new guidance following Wednesday's budget, dealers said.
Most market eyes -- satisfied for local facts and figures by the budget and recent PPI data -- turned to international markets for a clue as to which way share prices will go.
"People are looking around for something new now that the budget is out of the way and didn't come up with any real surprises," one dealer said.

But an overnight fall on Wall Street and jitters on London's FTSE 100 put a cap on local advances. Fears that New York shares may be in for a wave of selling knocked prices from their highs just before the close of trade.
The all-share index ended up 3.7 points at 7,171.6 as industrials gained 5.5 points to 8,373.7.
Blue chips had a mixed day with Iscor ending up five cents at 395 cents and De Beers unchanged at 161.00 rand.

More notable moves were to be found in smaller shares as confectioner Sweets From Heaven Ltd rose 38 cents to 280 cents after it sealed a deal to buy a 60 percent stake of U.S.-based Candy Headquarters Inc for an undisclosed sum.
Heaven said the U.S. deal, which had South African Reserve Bank approval, could result in up to 125 outlets being opened in the U.S. market by the end of the decade.

There was also a surge of market interest in transportation firm Quick Holdings Ltd (Quickco) which propelled the stock one cent higher to four cents but in heady volumes of more than 25 million shares.

The flurry of trade was sparked by comments Quickco made to shareholders at its annual general meeting in Durban on Wednesday. Dealers said trade was so heavy due to the firm's "penny share" status meaning traders were quickly getting in and out of the stock to capitalise on single cent rises in the price.
Gold shares had another weak day as the bullion price tottered and dealers speculated it could soon dip again to below the psychologically important $350 an ounce level.
The golds index shed 17.9 points to 1,429.6.

Futures contracts were mixed in early trade as the market digested Wednesday's budget, but as the day wore on volatility ahead of the contract close-out on Monday hit the market, as did worries Wall Street may see a sell-off.
The all-share March contract stood at 6,457/65 from 6,504 as the industrials contract was at 7,935/50 from 7,994. The golds contract was at 995/1,000 from 1,005.
